questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted something pretty close to Copenhagen, as I would be able to return home easily. Otherwise, I had been loads in Barcelona, and it seemed like a great opportunity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed some help with change of courses and getting my OLA signed, however UB were quite slow with this

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Family friend had an apartment I could borrow

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is alot of scammers, so you should be carefull with rentning something without seeing it in person.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I booked a time online in start september, and then I went in and signed a document while a member of the institution was there. Later we then had the oppotunity to change course, if we wanted

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Helped with how to choose and change courses

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It got all the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Consider taking courses from other faculties than Economics, I for instance took one from the Statistics Masters Degree, which was quite nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Generally, the level in UB seems to be quite a bit lower than in Copenhagen. The curriculum is smaller and the continous assesment system kinda removes the idea of good and bad grades, aswell as makes every subject pretty easy to pass.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was quite different, as in CPH we have big auditoriums for the teory part and then teaching assistents for the problem sets. However in UB it was just one teacher doing both, more fluid.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Macroeconomivs IV
Game Theory and Economic Application
Time Series Analysis
Financial Mathematics
World Economic History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Macro IV, Game Theory, Economic History and TSA

questions.answer: PRetty easy

questions.answer: Not that much

questions.answer: The fact that there are two offical languages both catalan and spanish

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Spending alot of time on local cafees etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You can take more than 30 ects point if you want to, as courses are quite easy and the professors are nice so you can take the exams when it fits you. 
There is public transport everywhere, but if you want to live close in the City, El Born, Eixample, Gracia etc,its gonna take 30-40 to get to school.
Enjoy of all the local stuff, cafees etc. Its really nice

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe travel down here and find and apartment instead of finding something online

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends that were made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My father died shortly before the exams, so that put some pressure on the exam period
